definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry is declared to be a profession and is defined as: (1) The examination of the human eye and its appendages; (2) The employment of any means for the measurement of the powers of visions, or any visual, muscular, neurological, interpretative, or anatomical anomaly of the visual process; (3) The prescribing or employment of lenses, prisms, frames, mountings, and visual training procedures; (4) The prescribing or administration, except by injection unless otherwise permitted by this chapter, of any pharmaceutical agent rational to the diagnosis and treatment of the human eye and its appendages; (5) The employment of any means or method for the correction, remedy, or relief of any insufficiency or abnormal condition of the visual process of the human eye and its appendages, provided the term 'any means or method' does not include surgeries, unless otherwise permitted by this chapter; (6) The removal of a superficial foreign body from the eye; (7) The prescribing of contact lenses, except by a physician licensed under chapter 36-4; (8) The use of intense pulsed light for the treatment of dry eye disease; and (9) Subject to the requirements set forth in §36-7-1.4...
definition_quote.quote: The practice of optometry is declared to be a profession and is defined as:

value: examination of the human eye and its appendages
measurement of powers of vision and visual anomalies
prescribing or employing lenses, prisms, frames, mountings, and visual training procedures
prescribing or administering pharmaceutical agents (except by injection unless otherwise permitted)

removal of a superficial foreign body from the eye
prescribing contact lenses
use of intense pulsed light for treatment of dry eye disease
intradermal injection of a paralytic agent (with prerequisites)

use of a local anesthetic in conjunction with primary removal of a pedunculated skin tag (with prerequisites)
selective laser trabeculoplasty (with prerequisites)
posterior capsulotomy using yttrium aluminum garnet laser (with prerequisites)

surgery_prohibited.quote: Nothing in this chapter may be construed to allow the performance, by an optometrist, of: (1) Intraocular injections; (2) Intraocular surgery; or (3) Refractive surgery.
